title: Sections over graphs extend by zero: the presheaf map from the etale sum presheaf to direct image
statement:
Let $\pi:U\to X$ be a finite etale morphism of schemes [def-weil-pbc-finite-etale-category, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring and $M$ a sheaf of $\Lambda_U$-modules on the small etale site $U_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For an object $V$ of $X_{\Et}$ write $V_U=V\times_XU$ [def-pc-fibre-product] with projections $p_V:V_U\to V$ and $q_V:V_U\to U$; $(V_U,q_V)$ is an object of $U_{\Et}$ and $(V_U,\,V_U\to V\to X)$ one of $X_{\Et}$ [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits]. For an $X$-morphism $\varphi:V\to U$ write $(V,\varphi)$ for $V$ regarded as an etale $U$-scheme and $\Gamma_\varphi=(\mathrm{id}_V,\varphi):V\to V_U$ for its graph. Then:

1. $(V,\varphi)$ is an object of $U_{\Et}$; $\Gamma_\varphi$ is a morphism $(V,\varphi)\to(V_U,q_V)$ of $U_{\Et}$; its image $\Gamma_\varphi(V)$ is open and closed in $V_U$, and $\Gamma_\varphi$ is an isomorphism of $V$ onto the open subscheme $\Gamma_\varphi(V)$.
2. For every $s\in M(V,\varphi)$ there is exactly one $e_\varphi(s)\in M(V_U,q_V)$ such that $M(\Gamma_\varphi)(e_\varphi(s))=s$ and the restriction of $e_\varphi(s)$ to the open subscheme $V_U\setminus\Gamma_\varphi(V)$ is $0$; the map $e_\varphi:M(V,\varphi)\to M(V_U,q_V)$ is $\Lambda$-linear.
3. Let $P_M$ be the presheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on $X_{\Et}$ of [def-weil-pbc-etale-sum-extension] for $v=\pi$: $P_M(V)=\bigoplus_{\varphi\in\operatorname{Hom}_X(V,U)}M(V,\varphi)$, the restriction along a morphism $a:V'\to V$ of $X_{\Et}$ sending the summand of $\varphi$ to the summand of $\varphi a$ by $M(a:(V',\varphi a)\to(V,\varphi))$. Then the maps
$$
c^p_{M,V}:P_M(V)\longrightarrow M(V_U,q_V)=(\pi_*M)(V),\qquad (s_\varphi)_\varphi\longmapsto\sum_\varphi e_\varphi(s_\varphi),
$$
with $\pi_*$ the direct image [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], form a morphism of presheaves of $\Lambda$-modules $c^p_M:P_M\to\pi_*M$ on $X_{\Et}$, and $c^p_M$ is natural in $M$: $\pi_*\alpha\circ c^p_M=c^p_{M'}\circ P_\alpha$ for every morphism $\alpha:M\to M'$ of sheaves of $\Lambda_U$-modules (with $P_\alpha=\bigoplus_\varphi\alpha_{(V,\varphi)}$). The key point for compatibility with restriction is that for $a:V'\to V$ in $X_{\Et}$ the preimage of $\Gamma_\varphi(V)$ under $a\times_X\mathrm{id}_U:V'_U\to V_U$ is $\Gamma_{\varphi a}(V')$.

source.place: Lemma 0F4L (lemma-shriek-into-star-separated-etale, line 11517), first paragraph of the proof (construction of the presheaf map j_{p!}F -> j_*F via the open and closed graph immersions Gamma_phi, there for separated etale j), using Schemes Lemma 01KT (schemes-lemma-section-immersion, literature/stacks-project/schemes.tex line 4275); here for finite etale pi and sheaves of Lambda-modules

proof.text: *The objects and the morphism $\Gamma_\varphi$.* Since $V\to X$ is etale and $\pi:U\to X$ is etale (it is finite etale [def-weil-pbc-finite-etale-category]), [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits] (1) applied to $u=\pi$ and the object $V\to X$ of $X_{\Et}$ shows that $q_V:V_U=V\times_XU\to U$ is etale, so $(V_U,q_V)$ is an object of $U_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]; applied to $u=(V\to X)$ and the object $\pi$ of $X_{\Et}$ it shows that $p_V:V_U\to V$ is etale. The $X$-morphism $\varphi:V\to U$ is a morphism between two schemes etale over $X$ commuting with the structure morphisms, hence etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation] (3); so $(V,\varphi)$ is an object of $U_{\Et}$. The graph $\Gamma_\varphi=(\mathrm{id}_V,\varphi)$ exists by the universal property of $V\times_XU$ [def-pc-fibre-product], since $(V\to X)\circ\mathrm{id}_V=\pi\circ\varphi$ ($\varphi$ is an $X$-morphism); it satisfies $p_V\circ\Gamma_\varphi=\mathrm{id}_V$ and $q_V\circ\Gamma_\varphi=\varphi$. The second identity says that $\Gamma_\varphi$ is a $U$-morphism $(V,\varphi)\to(V_U,q_V)$, i.e. a morphism of $U_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. This is the setting of the proof of Stacks 0F4L ('Evaluating both sides on $V\to X$ etale ... $\Gamma_\varphi=(1,\varphi):V\to V\times_XU$ over $U$').

source.place: Lemma 0F4L (lemma-shriek-into-star-separated-etale, line 11517), first paragraph of the proof (lines 11522-11546)

proof.text: *$\Gamma_\varphi$ is an open and closed immersion (clause 1).* The projection $p_V:V_U\to V$ is etale (step 1) and separated: it is the base change of $\pi$ along $V\to X$, and $\pi$ is finite, so $p_V$ is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence] (a); a finite morphism is affine by definition [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], and an affine morphism is separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence] (3). By step 1, $\Gamma_\varphi$ is a section of $p_V$: $p_V\circ\Gamma_\varphi=\mathrm{id}_V$. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-etale-section-clopen-immersion] (for the etale separated $p_V:V_U\to V$ and its section $\Gamma_\varphi$) gives: $\Gamma_\varphi$ is an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion] and a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], so $O:=\Gamma_\varphi(V)$ is open and closed in $V_U$ and $\Gamma_\varphi=j_O\circ\gamma$ with $j_O:O\to V_U$ the inclusion of the open subscheme and $\gamma:V\to O$ an isomorphism of schemes, whose inverse is $p_V\circ j_O$ (from $p_V\circ j_O\circ\gamma=\mathrm{id}_V$). In particular $\Gamma_\varphi\circ p_V\circ j_O=j_O\circ\gamma\circ\gamma^{-1}=j_O$. This is Stacks 0F4L ('It is open as it is a morphism between schemes etale over $U$ and it is closed as it is a section of a scheme separated over $V$'), with closedness from Schemes Lemma 01KT (schemes-lemma-section-immersion: a section of a separated morphism is a closed immersion), which is clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-section-clopen-immersion]; openness is clause (2) there (the section is etale, flat and a monomorphism), equivalent to Stacks' argument ($\Gamma_\varphi$ is a $U$-morphism between etale $U$-schemes, hence etale, hence open).

source.place: Lemma 0F4L (lemma-shriek-into-star-separated-etale, line 11517), first paragraph of the proof (lines 11522-11546); literature/stacks-project/schemes.tex, Lemma 01KT (lemma-section-immersion, line 4275)

proof.text: *Sections over $V_U$ split along $O$ and its complement.* Let $W=V_U\setminus O$, open (as $O$ is closed), with inclusion $j_W:W\to V_U$ of the open subscheme; $j_W$ and $\Gamma_\varphi$ are open immersions, hence etale [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation] (1), and $(W,q_V\circ j_W)$ is an object of $U_{\Et}$ (composite of etale morphisms, ibid. (2)). As $O\cup W=V_U$, the family $\{\Gamma_\varphi:(V,\varphi)\to(V_U,q_V),\ j_W:(W,q_Vj_W)\to(V_U,q_V)\}$ is a covering of $U_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], whose fibre products are scheme fibre products (ibid.). (i) An empty scheme $\varnothing$ with its unique morphism to $U$ (an open immersion onto the empty open, hence etale) is an object of $U_{\Et}$ covered by the empty family; the sheaf condition [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves] for it says $M(\varnothing)\to$ (empty product) is injective, so $M(\varnothing)=0$. (ii) If $T$ is a scheme with $a:T\to V$, $b:T\to W$ and $\Gamma_\varphi a=j_Wb$, every point of $T$ maps into $O\cap W=\varnothing$, so $T$ is empty; hence $V\times_{V_U}W$ and $W\times_{V_U}V$ are empty schemes [def-pc-fibre-product] and $M$ of them is $0$ by (i). (iii) $\Gamma_\varphi$ and $j_W$ are monomorphisms [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-monomorphism], so the two projections $V\times_{V_U}V\rightrightarrows V$ are equal (they become equal after composing with $\Gamma_\varphi$), and likewise for $W\times_{V_U}W$. The underlying presheaf of abelian groups of $M$ is an abelian sheaf on $U_{\Et}$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], and its sheaf condition for this covering says that $\rho:M(V_U,q_V)\to M(V,\varphi)\times M(W),\ t\mapsto(M(\Gamma_\varphi)t,\,M(j_W)t)$ is injective with image the pairs whose two restrictions to each of the four fibre products agree; by (ii) and (iii) this holds for every pair, so $\rho$ is bijective.

source.place: Lemma 0F4L (lemma-shriek-into-star-separated-etale, line 11517), first paragraph of the proof (lines 11522-11546) ('Thus for a section $s_\varphi$ ... there exists a unique section $s'_\varphi$ ... which pulls back to $s_\varphi$ by $\Gamma_\varphi$ and which restricts to zero on the complement of the image of $\Gamma_\varphi$'), written out

proof.text: *The $\Lambda$-module structures.* For an object $T$ of $U_{\Et}$ let $\iota_T:\Lambda\to\Lambda_U(T)$ be the ring map sending $\lambda$ to the image of the constant section $\lambda$ under the canonical map from the constant presheaf to its sheafification $\Lambda_U$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-weil-pbc-sheafification]; since the constant presheaf has identity restriction maps and the canonical map is a morphism of presheaves, every restriction map of $\Lambda_U$ sends $\iota_T(\lambda)$ to $\iota_{T'}(\lambda)$. $M(T)$ is a $\Lambda$-module through $\iota_T$, and by the semilinearity of the restriction maps of the $\Lambda_U$-module $M$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], every $M(g)$, $g$ a morphism of $U_{\Et}$, is $\Lambda$-linear; every component $\alpha_T$ of a morphism $\alpha$ of sheaves of $\Lambda_U$-modules is $\Lambda$-linear. These are the $\Lambda$-module structures on $M(V,\varphi)$, on $(\pi_*M)(V)=M(V_U,q_V)$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] and, summandwise, on $P_M(V)$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sum-extension]; the restriction maps of $P_M$ and of $\pi_*M$ (the maps $M(a_U)$, step 6) are $\Lambda$-linear, so both are presheaves of $\Lambda$-modules on $X_{\Et}$.

source.place: Lemma 0F4L (lemma-shriek-into-star-separated-etale, line 11517), first paragraph of the proof (lines 11522-11546) ('We prove this in the case of abelian sheaves'); the $\Lambda$-module case, with the module structures written out

proof.text: *Clause 2.* By step 3, $\rho$ is a bijection, and it is $\Lambda$-linear because $M(\Gamma_\varphi)$ and $M(j_W)$ are (step 4); so $\rho^{-1}$ is $\Lambda$-linear. For $s\in M(V,\varphi)$ put $e_\varphi(s)=\rho^{-1}(s,0)$. The conditions '$M(\Gamma_\varphi)(e)=s$ and the restriction $M(j_W)(e)$ of $e$ to the open subscheme $W=V_U\setminus\Gamma_\varphi(V)$ is $0$' say exactly $\rho(e)=(s,0)$, so $e_\varphi(s)$ is the unique element satisfying them, and $e_\varphi=\rho^{-1}\circ(s\mapsto(s,0))$ is $\Lambda$-linear.

source.place: Lemma 0F4L (lemma-shriek-into-star-separated-etale, line 11517), first paragraph of the proof (lines 11522-11546)

proof.text: *Graphs and base change along $a$.* Let $a:V'\to V$ be a morphism of $X_{\Et}$, $\varphi:V\to U$ an $X$-morphism, $\varphi'=\varphi a$, and $a_U=a\times_X\mathrm{id}_U:V'_U\to V_U$, the morphism with $p_V a_U=a\,p_{V'}$ and $q_Va_U=q_{V'}$ [def-pc-fibre-product]; it is a morphism $(V'_U,q_{V'})\to(V_U,q_V)$ of $U_{\Et}$, and $(\pi_*M)(a)=M(a_U)$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. Also $a$ is a morphism $(V',\varphi')\to(V,\varphi)$ of $U_{\Et}$. (i) $a_U\circ\Gamma_{\varphi'}=\Gamma_\varphi\circ a$: both have $p_V$-component $a$ and $q_V$-component $\varphi a$, so they agree by the uniqueness in [def-pc-fibre-product]. Hence $\Gamma_{\varphi'}(V')\subseteq a_U^{-1}(O)$. (ii) Conversely let $O'=a_U^{-1}(O)$, open in $V'_U$, with inclusion $\iota:O'\to V'_U$. Since $a_U\iota$ maps into $O$ it factors as $j_O\circ h$ [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme]; by step 2, $a_U\iota=\Gamma_\varphi p_Vj_Oh=\Gamma_\varphi p_Va_U\iota=\Gamma_\varphi\,a\,p_{V'}\iota$. Therefore $q_{V'}\iota=q_Va_U\iota=q_V\Gamma_\varphi a p_{V'}\iota=\varphi a\,p_{V'}\iota=q_{V'}\Gamma_{\varphi'}p_{V'}\iota$ and $p_{V'}\iota=p_{V'}\Gamma_{\varphi'}p_{V'}\iota$, so $\iota=\Gamma_{\varphi'}\circ p_{V'}\circ\iota$ [def-pc-fibre-product], and $O'=\iota(O')\subseteq\Gamma_{\varphi'}(V')$. So $a_U^{-1}(\Gamma_\varphi(V))=\Gamma_{\varphi a}(V')$, the key point named in the statement; equivalently $a_U$ maps $W'=V'_U\setminus\Gamma_{\varphi'}(V')$ into $W=V_U\setminus\Gamma_\varphi(V)$, and $a_U\circ j_{W'}=j_W\circ b$ for a unique $b:W'\to W$ [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme], a $U$-morphism ($q_Vj_Wb=q_Va_Uj_{W'}=q_{V'}j_{W'}$), hence a morphism of $U_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site].

source.place: Lemma 0F4L (lemma-shriek-into-star-separated-etale, line 11517), first paragraph of the proof (lines 11522-11546) (compatibility of the canonical map with restriction, left implicit in Stacks; written out by the agent)

proof.text: *Extension by zero commutes with restriction.* With the notation of step 6 and $s\in M(V,\varphi)$, put $t=M(a_U)(e_\varphi(s))\in M(V'_U,q_{V'})$. By step 6 (i), $M(\Gamma_{\varphi'})(t)=M(a_U\Gamma_{\varphi'})(e_\varphi s)=M(\Gamma_\varphi a)(e_\varphi s)=M(a)(M(\Gamma_\varphi)e_\varphi s)=M(a)(s)$, and by step 6 (ii), $M(j_{W'})(t)=M(a_Uj_{W'})(e_\varphi s)=M(b)(M(j_W)e_\varphi s)=M(b)(0)=0$ ($M$ is a contravariant functor on $U_{\Et}$). By the uniqueness in clause 2 (step 5) for $(V',\varphi')$: $M(a_U)(e_\varphi(s))=e_{\varphi a}(M(a)(s))$.

source.place: Lemma 0F4L (lemma-shriek-into-star-separated-etale, line 11517), first paragraph of the proof (lines 11522-11546)

proof.text: *Clause 3: $c^p_M$ is a morphism of presheaves of $\Lambda$-modules.* $c^p_{M,V}((s_\varphi)_\varphi)=\sum_\varphi e_\varphi(s_\varphi)$ is a finite sum (an element of the direct sum has finitely many nonzero components) of $\Lambda$-linear maps (step 5), hence well defined and $\Lambda$-linear. For $a:V'\to V$ in $X_{\Et}$ the restriction of $P_M$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sum-extension] sends $(s_\varphi)_\varphi$ to the family whose $\psi$-component is $\sum_{\varphi:\varphi a=\psi}M(a)(s_\varphi)$, and $(\pi_*M)(a)=M(a_U)$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. By step 7, $M(a_U)\big(\sum_\varphi e_\varphi(s_\varphi)\big)=\sum_\varphi e_{\varphi a}(M(a)s_\varphi)=\sum_\psi e_\psi\big(\sum_{\varphi a=\psi}M(a)s_\varphi\big)$, i.e. $(\pi_*M)(a)\circ c^p_{M,V}=c^p_{M,V'}\circ P_M(a)$. So $c^p_M:P_M\to\pi_*M$ is a morphism of presheaves of $\Lambda$-modules on $X_{\Et}$. This is the map $j_{p!}\mathcal F\to j_*\mathcal F$ of Stacks 0F4L for $j=\pi$.

source.place: Lemma 0F4L (lemma-shriek-into-star-separated-etale, line 11517), first paragraph of the proof (lines 11522-11546)

proof.text: *Naturality in $M$.* Let $\alpha:M\to M'$ be a morphism of sheaves of $\Lambda_U$-modules and $s\in M(V,\varphi)$. The components of $\alpha$ commute with the maps $M(g)$, $M'(g)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], so $M'(\Gamma_\varphi)(\alpha_{V_U}e_\varphi s)=\alpha_{(V,\varphi)}(M(\Gamma_\varphi)e_\varphi s)=\alpha_{(V,\varphi)}(s)$ and $M'(j_W)(\alpha_{V_U}e_\varphi s)=\alpha_W(0)=0$; by the uniqueness in clause 2 for $M'$, $\alpha_{V_U}(e_\varphi(s))=e'_\varphi(\alpha_{(V,\varphi)}(s))$. Summing over $\varphi$, and since $(\pi_*\alpha)_V=\alpha_{V_U}$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] and $(P_\alpha)_V=\bigoplus_\varphi\alpha_{(V,\varphi)}$: $\pi_*\alpha\circ c^p_M=c^p_{M'}\circ P_\alpha$.

lean.statement: theorem etale_graph_section_extension_map {X U : Scheme.{u}} (π : U ⟶ X) [IsFinite π] [Etale π] (Λ : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing Λ] : let L := MorphismProperty.Over.map (P := @Etale) ⊤ (inferInstance : Etale π) let B := MorphismProperty.Over.pullback @Etale ⊤ π let P := sheafToPresheaf U.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) ⋙ L.op.lan let D := Etale.lowerStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) π ⋙ sheafToPresheaf X.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) ∃ c : P ⟶ D, ∀ (M : Sheaf U.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ)) (W : U.Etale), let γ : W ⟶ B.obj (L.obj W) := (MorphismProperty.Over.mapPullbackAdj @Etale ⊤ π inferInstance trivial).unit.app W let e : M.obj.obj (op W) ⟶ M.obj.obj (op (B.obj (L.obj W))) := (L.op.lanUnit.app M.obj).app (op W) ≫ (c.app M).app (op (L.obj W)) ∀ (s : M.obj.obj (op W)) (t : M.obj.obj (op (B.obj (L.obj W)))), (M.obj.map γ.op t = s ∧ ∀ (T : U.Etale) (j : T ⟶ B.obj (L.obj W)), IsOpenImmersion j.left → Set.range j.left = (Set.range γ.left)ᶜ → M.obj.map j.op t = 0) ↔ t = e s
